In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanism underlying the regulation of RIG‐1 expression by IFNγ and how it affects de‐differentiation.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate glioma de‐differentiation.
the role of HMTs in regulating the expression of PGC‐1α and its target RIG‐I.

the HMTs G9a and PRTM‐1 regulate RIG‐I through a PGC‐1α mediated mechanism.
the HMTs G9a and PRTM‐1 regulate RIG‐I via PGC‐1a, and that the HMT G9a and the methyltransferase PRMT1 regulate RIG-I via PGC‐a.

The main takeaway from our work is that
IFN&grr; induced de‐differenciated state is regulated by concerted action of H3K9 histone methyltransferase G9a and arginine methyltransferases (PRMT)‐1.

IFN&g; treatment in glioma cells results in a counter‐active regulation of RIG‐1 and PGC‐α by HMTs G9a and Prmt‐1; with RIG‐I serving as a negative regulator of IFN&g;-induced de‐differentiation in glioma cells and PGC‐&agr; positively regulating RIG‐I.
